title: Direct image of an injective module is totally acyclic
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with its induced module direct image [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a sheaf of sets $K$ on a site $\mathcal T$ and an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal T}$-module $N$, put $\Gamma(K,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T)}(K,N_{\mathrm{sets}})$ with pointwise abelian-group operations, and put $H^q(K,N)=R^q\Gamma(K,-)(N)$, computed by injective resolutions in the module category [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If $I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module, then $$H^q(K,f_*I)=0$$ for every sheaf of sets $K$ on $\mathcal D$ and every $q>0$. Thus $f_*I$ is totally acyclic, where this means precisely the displayed vanishing for every $K$. No flatness of the structural ring map is assumed, and the geometric morphism need not come from a functor between the given sites.

proof.text: All module categories below have enough injectives: [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applies to each small site with its ring sheaf, and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] applies to the resulting Grothendieck abelian categories. The element sites used below are small by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]; the replacement sites are small by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-site-presentation]. Work in the common coefficient universe throughout. Thus the injective resolutions defining every right derived evaluation and global-section functor used below exist.

source.place: Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D); small slice and presentation sites: sites-modules.tex Tags 04IE and 03CR

proof.text: Fix a target sheaf of sets $K$ and put $B=f^{-1}K$. Write $r_K,r_B$ for module restriction to the small element sites presenting the slices. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], each restriction is exact and has an exact additive left adjoint $j_!$. It therefore preserves injectives, directly from the definition [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: a map $L\to r_KJ$ along a mono $L\hookrightarrow M$ corresponds to $j_!L\to J$; exactness makes $j_!L\to j_!M$ monic, so injectivity of $J$ extends it, and adjunction gives the required extension to $M$. The identical argument applies to $r_B$. For any module $N$, a section of $r_KN$ on the slice is a compatible family $n_{U,s}\in N(U)$ indexed by $s\in K(U)$, equivalently a natural map $K\to N_{\mathrm{sets}}$. This identifies the additive functors $\Gamma(K,-)$ and $\Gamma(\mathcal D/K,-)r_K$. Apply the exact, injective-preserving $r_K$ to an injective resolution of $N$; the two resulting section complexes agree. Hence $H^q(K,N)=R^q\Gamma(\mathcal D/K,-)(r_KN)$.

source.place: Section section-limp, definition of H^q(K,-); sites-modules.tex Tag 04IE (lemma-localize-ringed-topos), exact extension by zero

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-ordinary-square] with $A=K$. It supplies a ringed-topos morphism $f_K$ between the element-site slices and the natural MODULE isomorphism $r_Kf_*\cong f_{K*}r_B$. The restricted structural ring map is the one in that cited statement, so no scalar comparison is omitted. By step 2, $J=r_BI$ is injective. Substituting $N=f_*I$ in step 2 therefore reduces the desired vanishing to $R^q\Gamma(\mathcal D/K,-)(f_{K*}J)=0$, for $q>0$. Only the ordinary square is used; no derived direct-image composition or Leray theorem is assumed.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-site-presentation] to $f_K$. Obtain small finite-limit sites $\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$, ringed equivalences $g,e$, and a morphism of ringed sites $h$ induced by a continuous finite-limit-preserving $v:\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$, with $ef_K\cong hg$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport], the module functors $g_*,e_*$ are exact equivalences. In particular $J'=g_*J$ is injective: applying the exact inverse equivalence to a monomorphism and then the lifting property of $J$ proves its lifting property. The ringed commutativity gives $e_*f_{K*}J\cong h_*J'$ as modules, using the induced module direct image of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Indeed the right-adjoint comparison identifies underlying sheaves, and the commuting structural ring maps identify their scalar actions. For any module $P$ on the target slice, full faithfulness of $e_*$ and its preservation of the terminal sheaf identify $\Gamma(P)$ with $\Gamma(e_*P)$, including addition. Applying $e_*$ to an injective resolution gives an injective resolution, since it is an exact equivalence; thus this identification holds for all right derived global sections as well.

source.place: Tag 03CR (lemma-morphism-ringed-topoi-comes-from-morphism-ringed-sites), presentation and equivalence invariance; Tag 072Z first paragraph in sites-cohomology.tex

proof.text: The finite-limit site $\mathcal D'$ has a final object $T$, so $h_T$ is the terminal sheaf and module global sections are exactly evaluation at $T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-direct-image-injective-evaluation-acyclic] to $h$ and $J'$. Here the node's site $\mathcal C$ is $\mathcal D'$, its site $\mathcal D$ is $\mathcal C'$, its continuous functor $u$ is $v$, and its ring map $\rho:\mathcal O_{\mathcal D'}\to h_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C'}$ is the adjunct of $h^\sharp$. Since $h$ is the morphism of sites given by $v$, its direct image on sheaves of sets is $h_*=v^s$, $P\mapsto P\circ v$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3); the module direct image of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] has this underlying sheaf and the scalar action induced by $h^\sharp$, which on sections over $U$ is the action through $\rho_U$. So the module $h_*J'$ of step 4 is the node's $(h_*J')(U)=J'(v(U))$. Its continuous site-functor hypothesis is provided by step 4; its enough-injectives and size hypotheses are provided by step 1. Its conclusion at $U=T$ is $R^q\Gamma(T,-)(h_*J')=0$ for every $q>0$. Step 4 transports this vanishing to the target slice, and steps 2--3 identify it with $H^q(K,f_*I)$. Since $K$ was arbitrary, this is precisely the total acyclicity in the statement. No step asserts that $f_*I$ is injective or that the original ring map is flat.
